rounds.text: HB Portfolio Ltd trades at a remarkably low price-to-book ratio of 0.24x against a book value of ₹ 256 per share, with the market price sitting at ₹ 60.5 [E2]. The balance sheet exhibits exceptional strength, highlighted by a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x, borrowings reduced to ₹ 1.76 Cr, and a massive current ratio of 33.52x [E37, E38, E39]. Operational momentum has turned sharply positive in the short term, underscored by a 31% surge in trailing twelve-month sales growth and a staggering 302% explosion in compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. Furthermore, cash generation is extraordinary, featuring a cash conversion ratio of 36.71x backed by ₹ 10.28 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026, which proves that reported profits are entirely secured by hard cash [E34, E35]. Conceded: [E18], [E19], [E20], [E44], [E53].

HB Portfolio Ltd is burdened by a severe disconnect between its share price and its fundamental earning power, demonstrated by a discounted cash flow valuation model that places intrinsic value at Rs 34 per share compared to its market price of Rs 60.5, creating a negative margin of safety of 75.9% [E44, E45]. The business generates exceptionally weak returns on capital, highlighted by a 10-year median return on equity of just 2% [E26], a recent ROE of 0.1% [E13], and a low ROCE of 0.7% [E12]. Profit growth has deteriorated significantly over medium to long horizons, with compounded profit growth contracting by 27% over 10 years, 40% over 5 years, and 55% over 3 years [E18, E19, E20]. Operating margins are under pressure, dropping from 16% to 14% over the TTM period [E30] and turning negative at -1% in the September 2026 quarter [E31], alongside an inconsistent margin trend [E32, E33]. Furthermore, free cash flow was deeply negative at Rs -10.26 Cr in March 2026 [E36], and the rules-based screen explicitly scores the company at 42 out of 100 with a medium confidence sell rating due to decelerating earnings and extreme overvaluation [E54, E58, E60]. Conceded: the company maintains a very low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E37], trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.24x [E2], and delivered a strong 302% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21].

Conceded: intrinsic value is estimated at Rs 34 per share via DCF [E44]. However, the market price of Rs 60.5 is anchored to a deep tangible asset discount, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.24x compared to a sector benchmark of 7.06x [E2, E7]. While the bear points to low historical ROE figures [E26], the business maintains an exceptionally strong balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and borrowings down to Rs 1.76 Cr [E37, E39]. Furthermore, short-term liquidity is robust with a current ratio of 33.52x [E38], completely insulating the firm from solvency risks. On the operational front, profit growth has sharply accelerated with a 302% increase over the trailing twelve months [E21], alongside strong cash conversion where profits are fully backed by operating cash flows of Rs 10.28 Cr [E34, E35]. Finally, sales growth shows powerful recent momentum, expanding by 31% over the trailing twelve months and 22% year-over-year [E17, E55].

Conceded: the company maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x, borrowings of Rs 1.76 Cr, and a current ratio of 33.52x [E37, E38, E39]. However, pointing to a low price-to-book ratio of 0.24x against a sector benchmark of 7.06x ignores that this asset discount is fully justified by chronic underperformance, evidenced by a 10-year median ROE of just 2% and a median ROE of 0% over the last year [E2, E7, E26, E29]. While the bull highlights operating cash flows of Rs 10.28 Cr and high cash conversion for Mar 2026, free cash flow simultaneously plunged to a negative Rs -10.26 Cr, rendering that profit-backing illusory [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, citing TTM sales momentum of 31% masks a severe structural deterioration in profitability, highlighted by compounded profit growth of -55% over 3 years and a net profit collapse of 450% YoY [E17, E20, E57]. Finally, the reverse DCF proves that the current market price of Rs 60.5 already aggressively prices in 7.8% earnings growth despite a base case of 0.0% and an intrinsic DCF valuation of only Rs 34, leaving a -75.9% margin of safety and a rules-based SELL score of 42 out of 100 [E44, E45, E46, E54].
